Definition: from G3017; a Levite, i.e. descendant of Levi:--Levite.
BiblicalUsage: Leuḯtēs means a Levite — a small word with a sharp edge. In Luke 10:32, "And likewise a Levite"; and in John 1:19, "when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him". In Acts 4:36, "a Levite, [and] of the country of Cyprus".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Levite in the parable is the warning — he passed by on the other side, while the priesthood he belonged to was meant to serve, and Barnabas, a Levite, shows the other side by selling his field and laying the money at the apostles' feet.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
